ref_title: NIST AI 200-2 ipd: The TEVV-Athlon Framework for Evaluating AI Systems (initial public draft, August 2026)
summary_of_testing_content: Draft, non-prescriptive framework for planning an AI evaluation in four stages; defines metrology blocks, events and toolbox; says benchmarks, red teaming, user and field testing should be combined and that higher-risk systems need more rigorous measurement; a worked chatbot example uses user testing and red teaming; appendices say considerations are not prescriptive requirements (p. 27). Comment period reported as 7 Aug to 6 Oct 2026.

ref_title: NIST AI 700-2: Assessing Risks and Impacts of AI (ARIA) ARIA 0.1 Pilot Evaluation Report
summary_of_testing_content: Report of a pilot evaluating seven LLM applications from five submitters in three scenarios (TV Spoilers, Meal Planner, Pathfinder) using model testing, red teaming (51 red teamers) and field testing (19 testers), 508 sessions; results annotated and summarised with the CoRIx index; scores presented as illustrative; describes practice, imposes no duty.

ref_title: ARIA Program Evaluation Design Document (NIST, 20 December 2024)
summary_of_testing_content: Describes the three-level ARIA testbed (automated model testing, red teaming, field testing), scenario-based risk elicitation, five-step trained annotation, questionnaires and the tree-structured CoRIx measurement approach; states NIST does not define measurement thresholds; research programme design, not a binding standard.

ref_title: NIST SP 800-218A: Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models (SSDF Community Profile, July 2024)
summary_of_testing_content: Non-binding community profile adding AI model practices to SSDF; recommends including AI models in code testing policies (unit, integration, penetration, red teaming, adversarial), testing all models for vulnerabilities and retesting after retraining (PW.8.1, PW.8.2), scanning and testing acquired models before use (PW.4.4), scanning for malware and backdoors (PW.7.2), and periodic scanning, testing and audit after release (RV.1.2).

ref_title: OMB M-25-22: Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government (3 April 2025)
summary_of_testing_content: Memo to agencies on AI procurement. Agencies must, to the greatest extent practicable, test proposed solutions before award; contracts must give agencies ability to monitor and evaluate performance and risk, vendors must give access and time for evaluation using agency-defined data, and AI operated as an information system needs an authorization to operate before deployment; demonstrations, pre-deployment performance standards and periodic evaluation are should or encouraged. Excludes national security systems and intelligence community elements.

ref_title: America's AI Action Plan (White House, July 2025)
summary_of_testing_content: Policy plan, not a rule. Under Build an AI Evaluations Ecosystem it directs NIST/CAISI to support agency evaluation guidance, measurement science, shared evaluation practice and testbeds; also frontier-model national security evaluations (CAISI), a DOD proving ground, a hackathon to test AI systems, and a possible deepfake evaluation guideline. Sets no testing duty on private developers.
